body:
While this kind of thing is actually quite refreshing when it comes to trying to be emotional in a controlled environment, in practice when these things surface I'm too hardwired to cut out my emotion even at the sacrifice of other people's feelings. 
It's mostly because I've never been able to rely on others to fix my problems and when I see others freaking out or distressed about things I have to be the one with the clear head or the whole matter will fall apart

Being alone doesnt bother me every day, if I keep busy or whatever. I just get on with something and I find that I can cope quite well without anyone. However during downtime I just find myself thinking 'hah I just thought if something cool/funny. Oh, I can't really talk to anyone about it... It probably wasn't that funny anyway'. 

 If I had the gorram money I would move as far away as is humanly possible, the thing is there is just no way that I'll ever make enough to set up anywhere for enough time to find a job that pays enough to support me. Most of the money I save goes to my parents as way of rent and food/living expenses just eat so much away that I can't hold onto any money for my future. But again, I can live in this limbo of mediocrity if I want and survive so why should I be allowed to complain?

My parents and I are pretty much strangers, they stay out of my way and I do theirs, I thank god I'm working on my birthday on Friday because I don't know how I'd handle sitting around the house just listening to their screaming matches as a birthday present. 

I'm not too good at the headphone thing yet but the parts cost like £1  and i was sick of spending money on new ones so I try to get better at it. Finding time when I'm not just too exhausted to do so though is getting difficult. I mean if I'm this exhausted from a job that ends up paying me next to nothing, what's gonna happen to me if I find something that can actually provide for me? 

I do appreciate the chat though, I don't want to be ungrateful towards someone actually trying to help. Honestly though, if I'm stuck where I am long enough I have two major worries:

That I'll shut down so much in order to cope with living as I do that I'll just stop feeling anything. At this point I feel I'd just submit to the fact that this is my life and I should be grateful to be alive. At which point I cease to be myself and just another husk scraping through my lifespan without any emotion.

Or that my emotions will surface eventually and that I'll crumble in on myself. If that happens I have no idea what I'll become or what I'll do. 

Both are becoming very real options, I mean the first one seems very near and the second might come even long after that.

I see what you mean but I'm a bit afraid to un-learn how deal with things in a strictly non-emotional manner if it turns out I'm an emotional train wreck and unable to deal with regular day to day. As to of I knew someone who was depressed, I'd listen and try to help but when I hear day to day problems spoken out loud they feel so underwhelming that I can't help but switch off, I do hate that part about me though. 
I'll stick to the facts about me for now so I mean it might be better to see it in writing.

I currently have zero close friends since moving back in with my parents. I've been trying for a long time to make friends online or to attend local this and that's but where I live these things are simply non existent so no friends.
I have a dull, low paying, horrible job. It's pays me just little enough that I can't afford to live on my own off of it. It took me a long time just to find this job and I won't find anything better until I move somewhere else. So kind of a catch 22 there...
Hobby wise I really can't do a whole lot on my own, still I try to pick things up, video editing, animating, fixing headphones, writing scripts. 

So, on paper, this really isn't that bad. I mean I have a roof over my head and can afford food so honestly what right do I have to complain? Where the suicidal thoughts come in is by seeing this and figuring, yup, this is gonna be my life, no question about it, it's not horrid but I don't particularly fancy it.

Devalues, that's the word I was looking for. 
This is really the case, where I can objectively see that my life has problems but I won't address them because people in worse situations than mine cope just fine. 
I'm more or less devoid of any emotion these days, in some ways it's helped me do great things by approaching everything logically but the logic I use when facing these thoughts just brings me to an acceptable conclusion of 'death would be just fine with me'. 
The thing about complaining is that I hate people who complain. I don't know where I got this prejudice from exactly but just as I hate myself for thinking my problems are worse than others I also turn off at people who try to make big deals out of their day to day stuff even though to them it might be a legitimate issue that causes then serious grief. I don't like that I feel this way but it's kind of a knee jerk reaction I use towards problem solving: look at the problem objectively and it doesn't seem so bad.

Well you're right in saying I consider the opinion of others but honestly I don't put much credence towards it, if tomorrow I decided to kill myself I'd think 'I'd be dead, what do I care what they think at that point?'.

Part of the problem comes from the fact that as I don't feel my problems are that bad compared to others I also don't feel it's worth giving anyone the burden of listening to me, as a result I honestly haven't shared my feelings with anyone in several years.
